reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a PancakeSwap/MetaMask front-running or sniper trading bot through an external download link and instructions to deploy a contract, fund it with BNB, approve wallet interactions, and pay gas. It presents automated buying and selling with claims including a 90% return flow, several-hundred-BNB earnings, an around-50x result, and possible earnings of 1000 BNB per day. The linked software, contract code, wallet permissions, and transaction outcomes are not verified.

Download Links └ GHOST sniper BOT: https://clck.ru/afxbU
the next. Step in this process is just funding your contract
Send some funds to that contract that we just created
The action button then engages all the constructors. That I built in as far as engaging the pancake router. It automatically buys and sells for. You

opening.argument: The presentation does not state that returns are guaranteed or that viewers must trust an unverifiable promise. It describes a tool as free, gives viewers time to pause and follow the steps, and closes with a plainly non-assured sign-off. The reported results are framed as the speaker's experience rather than a universal outcome: he says he has had good luck and describes what happened in his demonstration. That is compatible with a risky, user-controlled experiment whose results depend on market conditions, not a promise that every viewer will profit.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats every operational step as deceptive solicitation, but those steps can equally be a transparent description of how a user-controlled blockchain tool works. Its cited earnings statements are presented as the speaker's account, not proof that viewers are promised the same result. The download reference alone establishes availability of a tool, not that the tool is fraudulent.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the tool free and describing it as an experiment does not neutralize the concrete profit pitch. The speaker says the bot will front-run retail investors, return 90% to the wallet, and can produce 1000 BNB a day. Those are not merely neutral risk disclosures; they are the claimed financial outcome attached to funding and activating the contract.

opening.argument: The video's central activity is an operational programming demonstration. It walks through creating a Solidity file, compiling it in Remix, connecting injected Web3, deploying a contract, inspecting the resulting address, and using a function manager. The speaker explains the wrapped-BNB input address, PancakeSwap router, and contract workflow while showing the interface. That is recognizable as a technology tutorial and demonstration, even if the subject is speculative trading. Explaining how a tool is configured and operated does not by itself establish that the creator is certifying its safety or guaranteeing its results.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes the financial context but does not displace the video's tutorial structure. The speaker explains code, compilation, deployment, and interface state in sequence. A tutorial can demonstrate a controversial or risky technology without becoming a verified endorsement of every result described during the demonstration.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely how the alleged opportunity is made actionable. The demonstration tells viewers to fund the deployed contract, click its action control, and expect automated purchases and sales. Technical detail does not change that the instruction is tied to claimed profits and front-running retail investors.

opening.argument: At most, the material promotes access to a software tool and explains a blockchain service workflow. The description calls the bot free and supplies a download link; the transcript does not ask viewers for a password, seed phrase, login credentials, or a downline. It also does not describe recurring recruitment or referral income. The visible workflow is a user choosing to connect a wallet, deploy a contract, and pay network gas, rather than handing credentials to a salesperson. Those facts leave important scam mechanisms unestablished and support treating this as ordinary software or service promotion, without certifying the tool's safety.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A download link and blockchain transaction are not enough to prove a scam mechanism. The supplied material does not show credential harvesting, recruitment, or a promised referral structure. The prosecution's description of wallet activity demonstrates what the tutorial says to do, but does not establish that the destination controlled the wallet or that the software was malicious.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing-credential argument overlooks the mechanism actually presented: viewers are told to fund a contract, sign another transaction, and activate automated trading. The speaker then claims a 50x result, 90% transfers back, and potentially 1000 BNB per day. A scam need not request a seed phrase or recruit a downline when its pitch directs funds into a contract while asserting extraordinary returns.
